sanskrit: sa gatvā pitaraṃ tasyā varayām āsa tāṃ tadā paryapṛcchat tatas tasyāḥ pitaraṃ cātmakāraṇāt
english: He went to her father and sought her hand, then questioned her father about his own purposes and conditions.

sanskrit: sa ca taṃ pratyuvācedaṃ dāśarājo mahīpatim jātamātraiva me deyā varāya varavarṇinī hṛdi kāmas tu me kaś cit taṃ nibodha janeśvara
english: The fisher-king replied to that lord of the earth: "This fair-complexioned girl is mine to give in marriage the moment she is asked; but there is a certain wish in my heart — hear it, O lord of men."

sanskrit: yadīmāṃ dharmapatnīṃ tvaṃ mattaḥ prārthayase 'nagha satyavāg asi satyena samayaṃ kuru me tataḥ
english: "If you desire this girl as your lawful wife, O sinless one, you are known as a speaker of truth — therefore make a solemn compact with me in truth."

sanskrit: samayena pradadyāṃ te kanyām aham imāṃ nṛpa na hi me tvatsamaḥ kaś cid varo jātu bhaviṣyati
english: "Upon a pledge I will give you this maiden, O king; for no bridegroom equal to you shall ever come to me again."

sanskrit: śaṃtanur uvāca śrutvā tava varaṃ dāśa vyavasyeyam ahaṃ na vā dātavyaṃ cet pradāsyāmi na tv adeyaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: Śantanu said: "Having heard your condition, O fisher-man, I will consider whether I can grant it or not. What can be given I will give; what cannot be given I will never give under any circumstances."

sanskrit: dāśa uvāca asyāṃ jāyeta yaḥ putraḥ sa rājā pṛthivīpatiḥ tvad ūrdhvam abhiṣektavyo nānyaḥ kaś cana pārthiva
english: The fisherman said: "Whatever son is born of her shall be consecrated king and lord of the earth after you — no other, O king."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca nākāmayata taṃ dātuṃ varaṃ dāśāya śaṃtanuḥ śarīrajena tīvreṇa dahyamāno 'pi bhārata
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Śantanu did not wish to grant that boon to the fisherman, O Bhārata, even though he burned intensely with desire born of the body.

sanskrit: sa cintayann eva tadā dāśakanyāṃ mahīpatiḥ pratyayād dhāstinapuraṃ śokopahatacetanaḥ
english: That great king, dwelling only in thought on the fisher's daughter, returned to Hāstinapura with his mind struck by grief.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cic chocantaṃ śaṃtanuṃ dhyānam āsthitam putro devavrato 'bhyetya pitaraṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Then one day his son Devavrata, approaching his father who was grieving and sunk in brooding thought, spoke these words to him.

sanskrit: sarvato bhavataḥ kṣemaṃ vidheyāḥ sarvapārthivāḥ tat kimartham ihābhīkṣṇaṃ pariśocasi duḥkhitaḥ dhyāyann iva ca kiṃ rājan nābhibhāṣasi kiṃ cana
english: "All the kings of the earth are subject to your welfare; for what reason then do you grieve here constantly, O sorrowful one? And why, as if lost in meditation, do you say nothing at all, O king?"

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa putreṇa śaṃtanuḥ pratyabhāṣata asaṃśayaṃ dhyānaparaṃ yathā māttha tathāsmy uta
english: Thus addressed by his son, Śantanu replied: "Without doubt I am indeed absorbed in brooding, just as you say."

sanskrit: apatyaṃ nas tvam evaikaḥ kule mahati bhārata anityatā ca martyānām ataḥ śocāmi putraka
english: "In this great lineage, you alone are our offspring, O Bhārata; and mortal men are impermanent — for this reason I grieve, my son."

sanskrit: kathaṃ cit tava gāṅgeya vipattau nāsti naḥ kulam asaṃśayaṃ tvam evaikaḥ śatād api varaḥ sutaḥ
english: "Should any misfortune befall you, O son of the Ganges, our lineage is extinct; you alone, without doubt, are worth a hundred sons."

sanskrit: na cāpy ahaṃ vṛthā bhūyo dārān kartum ihotsahe saṃtānasyāvināśāya kāmaye bhadram astu te anapatyataikaputratvam ity āhur dharmavādinaḥ
english: "Nor am I willing to take a wife again without purpose; yet for the preservation of the lineage I desire it — may it go well with you. Those who speak of dharma call having only one son the same as being sonless."

sanskrit: agnihotraṃ trayo vedā yajñāś ca sahadakṣiṇāḥ sarvāṇy etāny apatyasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm
english: "The agnihotra sacrifice, the three Vedas, and all the yajñas together with their dakṣiṇās — all these do not equal a sixteenth part of the merit of having offspring."

sanskrit: evam eva manuṣyeṣu syāc ca sarvaprajāsv api yad apatyaṃ mahāprājña tatra me nāsti saṃśayaḥ eṣā trayī purāṇānām uttamānāṃ ca śāśvatī
english: "So it is likewise among men and among all creatures — this is the eternal triad of the ancients and of the best: that offspring is supreme. In this, O greatly wise one, I have no doubt."

sanskrit: tvaṃ ca śūraḥ sadāmarṣī śastranityaś ca bhārata nānyatra śastrāt tasmāt te nidhanaṃ vidyate 'nagha
english: "And you are a hero, ever proud, ever engaged with weapons, O Bhārata; your death, O sinless one, can come from nowhere other than a weapon."

sanskrit: so 'smi saṃśayam āpannas tvayi śānte kathaṃ bhavet iti te kāraṇaṃ tāta duḥkhasyoktam aśeṣataḥ
english: "Thus I am fallen into doubt: should you be at peace, how will it be? I have told you in full, my dear son, the entire cause of my grief."

sanskrit: tatas tat kāraṇaṃ jñātvā kṛtsnaṃ caivam aśeṣataḥ devavrato mahābuddhiḥ prayayāv anucintayan
english: Then, having learned the entire cause in full, Devavrata of great intelligence departed, pondering it deeply.

sanskrit: abhyagacchat tadaivāśu vṛddhāmātyaṃ pitur hitam tam apṛcchat tadābhyetya pitus tac chokakāraṇam
english: He went quickly to seek the aged minister who was loyal to his father, and approaching him, inquired about the cause of his father's grief.

sanskrit: tasmai sa kurumukhyāya yathāvat paripṛcchate varaṃ śaśaṃsa kanyāṃ tām uddiśya bharatarṣabha
english: To that chief of the Kurus who asked him properly, the minister recounted in full the boon demanded, naming the maiden in question, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tato devavrato vṛddhaiḥ kṣatriyaiḥ sahitas tadā abhigamya dāśarājānaṃ kanyāṃ vavre pituḥ svayam
english: Then Devavrata, accompanied by senior Kṣatriyas, went himself to the fisher-king and sought the maiden on behalf of his father.

sanskrit: taṃ dāśaḥ pratijagrāha vidhivat pratipūjya ca abravīc cainam āsīnaṃ rājasaṃsadi bhārata
english: The fisherman received him according to due rite and honored him, then spoke to him as he sat in the royal assembly, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tvam eva nāthaḥ paryāptaḥ śaṃtanoḥ puruṣarṣabha putraḥ putravatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ kiṃ nu vakṣyāmi te vacaḥ
english: "You alone are a sufficient guardian for Śantanu, O bull among men; you are the best son among those who have sons — what then shall I say to you?"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato vivāhe nirvṛtte sa rājā śaṃtanur nṛpaḥ tāṃ kanyāṃ rūpasaṃpannāṃ svagṛhe saṃnyaveśayat
english: Vaiśampāyana said: After the marriage was concluded, King Śantanu installed that maiden of surpassing beauty in his own home.

sanskrit: tataḥ śāṃtanavo dhīmān satyavatyām ajāyata vīraś citrāṅgado nāma vīryeṇa manujān ati
english: Then the wise son of Śantanu was born of Satyavatī — the hero named Citrāṅgada, who surpassed all men in valour.

sanskrit: athāparaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ satyavatyāṃ punaḥ prabhuḥ vicitravīryaṃ rājānaṃ janayām āsa vīryavān
english: Then again the mighty lord begot upon Satyavatī another great archer, Prince Vicitravīrya.

sanskrit: aprāptavati tasmiṃś ca yauvanaṃ bharatarṣabha sa rājā śaṃtanur dhīmān kāladharmam upeyivān
english: While Vicitravīrya had not yet reached youth, O bull of the Bharatas, the wise King Śantanu submitted to the law of time and passed away.

sanskrit: svargate śaṃtanau bhīṣmaś citrāṅgadam ariṃdamam sthāpayām āsa vai rājye satyavatyā mate sthitaḥ
english: With Śantanu gone to heaven, Bhīṣma, abiding by Satyavatī's counsel, established the enemy-taming Citrāṅgada upon the throne.

sanskrit: sa tu citrāṅgadaḥ śauryāt sarvāṃś cikṣepa pārthivān manuṣyaṃ na hi mene sa kaṃ cit sadṛśam ātmanaḥ
english: But Citrāṅgada, through his valour, held all other kings in contempt; he considered no human being his equal.

sanskrit: taṃ kṣipantaṃ surāṃś caiva manuṣyān asurāṃs tathā gandharvarājo balavāṃs tulyanāmābhyayāt tadā tenāsya sumahad yuddhaṃ kurukṣetre babhūva ha
english: As he was thus scorning gods, men, and asuras alike, a powerful Gandharva king bearing the same name came against him; and a mighty battle between them took place on the field of Kurukṣetra.

sanskrit: tayor balavatos tatra gandharvakurumukhyayoḥ nadyās tīre hiraṇvatyāḥ samās tisro 'bhavad raṇaḥ
english: Between those two powerful ones — the Gandharva chief and the chief of the Kurus — the battle raged for three years on the bank of the river Hiraṇvatī.

sanskrit: tasmin vimarde tumule śastravṛṣṭisamākule māyādhiko 'vadhīd vīraṃ gandharvaḥ kurusattamam
english: In that tumultuous clash, thick with a rain of weapons, the Gandharva, superior in magical power, slew the foremost of the Kurus.

sanskrit: citrāṅgadaṃ kuruśreṣṭhaṃ vicitraśarakārmukam antāya kṛtvā gandharvo divam ācakrame tataḥ
english: Having slain Citrāṅgada, best of the Kurus, whose bow and arrows were varied and marvelous, the Gandharva then ascended to heaven.

sanskrit: tasmin nṛpatiśārdūle nihate bhūrivarcasi bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo rājan pretakāryāṇy akārayat
english: When that tiger among kings, of great splendour, was slain, Bhīṣma son of Śantanu performed the funeral rites, O king.

sanskrit: vicitravīryaṃ ca tadā bālam aprāptayauvanam kururājye mahābāhur abhyaṣiñcad anantaram
english: And the mighty-armed Bhīṣma then immediately consecrated the child Vicitravīrya, who had not yet come of age, to the Kuru kingship.

sanskrit: vicitravīryas tu tadā bhīṣmasya vacane sthitaḥ anvaśāsan mahārāja pitṛpaitāmahaṃ padam
english: Vicitravīrya, abiding by Bhīṣma's counsel, then administered the realm that had been his father's and grandfather's, O great king.

sanskrit: sa dharmaśāstrakuśalo bhīṣmaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ nṛpaḥ pūjayām āsa dharmeṇa sa cainaṃ pratyapālayat
english: That king, skilled in the science of dharma, honored Bhīṣma son of Śantanu with righteous conduct, and Bhīṣma in turn protected him.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca hate citrāṅgade bhīṣmo bāle bhrātari cānagha pālayām āsa tad rājyaṃ satyavatyā mate sthitaḥ
english: Vaiśampāyana said: When Citrāṅgada was slain, O sinless one, Bhīṣma, abiding by Satyavatī's counsel, administered that kingdom on behalf of his young brother.

sanskrit: saṃprāptayauvanaṃ paśyan bhrātaraṃ dhīmatāṃ varam bhīṣmo vicitravīryasya vivāhāyākaron matim
english: Seeing that his brother, the best among the wise, had come of age, Bhīṣma resolved to arrange the marriage of Vicitravīrya.

sanskrit: atha kāśipater bhīṣmaḥ kanyās tisro 'psaraḥsamāḥ śuśrāva sahitā rājan vṛṇvatīr vai svayaṃ varam
english: Then Bhīṣma heard, O king, that three daughters of the king of Kāśī, equal in beauty to apsarases, were holding a svayaṃvara to choose their own husbands.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rathināṃ śreṣṭho rathenaikena varmabhṛt jagāmānumate mātuḥ purīṃ vārāṇasīṃ prati
english: Then that best of chariot-warriors, clad in armour, set out with a single chariot, with his mother's permission, toward the city of Vārāṇasī.

sanskrit: tatra rājñaḥ samuditān sarvataḥ samupāgatān dadarśa kanyās tāś caiva bhīṣmaḥ śaṃtanunandanaḥ
english: There Bhīṣma, the son of Śantanu, saw the assembled kings who had gathered from all directions, and the maidens as well.

sanskrit: kīrtyamāneṣu rājñāṃ tu nāmasv atha sahasraśaḥ bhīṣmaḥ svayaṃ tadā rājan varayām āsa tāḥ prabhuḥ
english: While the names of thousands of kings were being proclaimed, Bhīṣma himself, that mighty lord, then chose those maidens, O king.

sanskrit: uvāca ca mahīpālān rājañ jaladaniḥsvanaḥ ratham āropya tāḥ kanyā bhīṣmaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ
english: And Bhīṣma, best of warriors, whose voice was like the roar of a rain-cloud, having placed those maidens on his chariot, addressed the assembled kings, O king.

sanskrit: āhūya dānaṃ kanyānāṃ guṇavadbhyaḥ smṛtaṃ budhaiḥ alaṃkṛtya yathāśakti pradāya ca dhanāny api
english: "The gift of maidens after inviting worthy suitors, adorning the bride, and giving wealth according to one's means — this is ordained by the wise as one form of marriage."

sanskrit: prayacchanty apare kanyāṃ mithunena gavām api vittena kathitenānye balenānye 'numānya ca
english: "Others give a maiden in exchange for a pair of cattle, others for a stated price, others by force, and others by obtaining consent."

sanskrit: pramattām upayānty anye svayam anye ca vindate aṣṭamaṃ tam atho vitta vivāhaṃ kavibhiḥ smṛtam
english: "Some take a maiden unawares, while others win her by mutual desire — that eighth form, O know well, is named among the sages."

sanskrit: svayaṃvaraṃ tu rājanyāḥ praśaṃsanty upayānti ca pramathya tu hṛtām āhur jyāyasīṃ dharmavādinaḥ
english: "The svayaṃvara is praised and resorted to by Kṣatriyas; but those who speak of dharma declare that a bride seized by force after vanquishing opponents is the highest form of marriage for the warrior class."

sanskrit: tā imāḥ pṛthivīpālā jihīrṣāmi balād itaḥ te yatadhvaṃ paraṃ śaktyā vijayāyetarāya vā sthito 'haṃ pṛthivīpālā yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ
english: "These maidens here I intend to carry away by force, O lords of the earth. Exert yourselves to the utmost, whether for victory or otherwise — I stand resolved for battle, O kings."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahīpālān kāśirājaṃ ca vīryavān sarvāḥ kanyāḥ sa kauravyo ratham āropayat svakam āmantrya ca sa tān prāyāc chīghraṃ kanyāḥ pragṛhya tāḥ
english: Having thus addressed the kings and the king of Kāśī, the valiant Kaurava placed all the maidens on his chariot, bade farewell to them all, and swiftly departed, the maidens in his possession.

sanskrit: tatas te pārthivāḥ sarve samutpetur amarṣitāḥ saṃspṛśantaḥ svakān bāhūn daśanto daśanacchadān
english: Then all those kings sprang up in fury, slapping their own arms and biting their lips.

sanskrit: teṣām ābharaṇāny āśu tvaritānāṃ vimuñcatām āmuñcatāṃ ca varmāṇi saṃbhramaḥ sumahān abhūt
english: As they rushed forward hastily, removing their ornaments and putting on their armour, there was a great tumult.

sanskrit: tārāṇām iva saṃpāto babhūva janamejaya bhūṣaṇānāṃ ca śubhrāṇāṃ kavacānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: There was a shower as of falling stars, O Janamejaya, of bright ornaments and coats of armour on all sides.

sanskrit: savarmabhir bhūṣaṇais te drāg bhrājadbhir itas tataḥ sakrodhāmarṣajihmabhrūsakaṣāyadṛśas tathā
english: With their armour and ornaments gleaming swiftly in every direction, and with brows furrowed in anger and indignation and eyes red with rage, they stood thus.
